messages.text: That needs revision - placing the modules aligned with global x-y will not result in stable transverse / longitudinal resolution, particularly for non-squared pixels … instead, try to arrange single, eventually double and quad modules similar to the quad-only, still reducing pixel overlap … from your proposal you can keep the innermost ring - if more silicon overlap is needed to guarantee hermeticity, increase to 15-20

I’ll revise the optimization around local radial and tangential module orientations, keeping the innermost ring and trying single, double and quad modules. I’ll use 15% overlap as the preferred limit and allow up to 20% where coverage requires it, then rerun the geometry and ACTS checks.

The earlier search minimized overlap without constraining the pixel axes relative to the disc’s radial and tangential directions. I’ll add that constraint and retain the earlier figures as superseded evidence.

The ACTS preflight found changed setup fingerprints, so I’m rechecking the installed runtime before using it.

The ACTS runtime is verified. I’m testing concentric single-module rings first, then double and quad variants with explicit inactive chip seams. The revised checks will cover both hermeticity and how the pixel measurement axes vary around the disc.

A concentric single-module layout now passes the straight-ray coverage certificates, with about 15.6% overall and 17.5% annular overlap at the first disc. The double and quad variants tested so far leave active gaps at chip seams.

I’m retaining those rejected variants and checking the selected layout with native ACTS. I’ll also report the remaining axis variation across each flat module.
All 15 geometry and covariance controls passed. The native audit stopped at its input-consistency check, so I’m checking the disc datums before allowing transport to run.

The datum difference was floating-point roundoff between the two detector ends; their positions are unchanged. The revised audit is running with the actual source datums preserved.

The selected layout keeps tangential and radial axes at module centres. Its corner-axis variation is largest in the retained inner ring, so the report will quantify that limit.

Native ACTS passed: 324 matched tracks for each layout, six exhaustive controls, and no missed target discs or intersection/ID mismatches.

The revised layout stays below 20% overlap at every disc. It still needs a larger support envelope, and the inherited shared-service packing still fails. I’m preparing the updated figures and PR #41 description with those limits visible.

The revised figures are ready. The selected layout has 359 chips per disc, compared with 448 in the quad baseline, and retains the 18-module inner ring.

I’m finishing the documentation checks before pushing the revision to PR #41.

PR #41 is updated and pushed with the radial layout, rejected mixed-family controls, and new comparison figures. The hosted checks are now the last verification step.

This revision has its own session record. Its final token counters will be recovered after the turn closes, keeping them separate from the original implementation’s accounting.

The hosted build passed for the radial revision. I’m recording that result and closing the scientific task log.

The post-turn accounting follow-up will recover this revision’s final counters and pause itself first, preventing duplicate scheduled runs.
The scientific build is green. The final logging-only commit is going through hosted validation; the published figures and numerical evidence remain unchanged.

PR41’s revised layout and final hosted build have passed. The layout keeps the inner ring, uses radial/tangential module axes, and stays below 20% overlap across all discs. I’m scheduling the one-time token recovery to run after this turn closes.

Revised and pushed to [PR41](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/41).

![Before and revised disc layouts]([redacted]

The revised layout uses **359 single modules in nine rings**, with tangential/radial axes and the original 18-module inner ring retained. Tested double/quad combinations left inactive-seam holes or exceeded the overlap limit.

Overlap is **15.6% whole-silicon / 17.5% within the annulus** on the first disc, reaching **19.48%** across all discs. The non-square-pixel covariance control confirms consistent axes at module centres.

All 16 controls, native ACTS checks and hosted builds passed. Guard dimensions and service routing still need engineering review.

Final token recovery is scheduled after this turn closes.
